# This Is What Happens When You Get a Kidney Transplant

**Format:** Zack D. Films style, 3D close-up animation, calm narrator · **Words:** 251 · **Est. runtime:** ~95-104 s

## Narration

This is what happens when you get a kidney transplant. Your own kidneys have stopped working. So you're getting a new one from a donor. But it doesn't go where your old ones are.

Your kidneys sit high up, tucked against your back. That spot is hard to reach. Instead, the surgeon makes a cut low on one side of your belly. The new kidney is placed down here, just above your leg.

Its artery and vein are sewn onto the big blood vessels running to that leg. Blood rushes in. Next, its drainage tube, the ureter, is stitched onto your bladder. A tiny plastic stent often holds it open while it heals. The whole operation takes a few hours. And often, the new kidney starts making urine almost right away.

But what happens to your old kidneys? Usually... nothing. They stay exactly where they are. Taking them out would mean more surgery, and more risk. And one working kidney is enough. They're only removed if they cause trouble, like infections, stones, or high blood pressure.

So you wake up with three kidneys. Two that don't work. One that does.

You take anti-rejection medicine every day, for as long as the new kidney lasts. And eventually, it can wear out. When it does, you can get another transplant. And once again, the old ones usually stay.

In 2025, a man in India got his third kidney transplant. He now has five kidneys inside his body. Only one of them works.

## Sources

- Mayo Clinic, Kidney transplant: https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/kidney-transplant/about/pac-20384777 (lower-abdomen placement, vessels and ureter, own kidneys left in place unless they cause BP, stones, pain or infection)
- NHS Blood and Transplant, Kidney transplant surgery: https://www.nhsbt.nhs.uk/organ-transplantation/kidney/at-the-transplant-centre/kidney-transplant-surgery/ (lower-abdomen incision, right or left groin, stent, 2-4 h, own kidneys usually left)
- NIDDK, Kidney transplant: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/kidney-disease/kidney-failure/kidney-transplant (lower abdomen near the groin, 3-4 h, may work right away or take a few days, daily medicines)
- National Kidney Foundation: https://www.kidney.org/kidney-topics/kidney-transplant-surgery and https://www.kidney.org/kidney-topics/kidney-transplant (own kidneys generally not removed, meds for as long as the kidney works, graft lifespan)
- Wikipedia, Kidney transplantation: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney_transplantation (iliac vessels, nephrectomy increases surgical morbidity, usually functions immediately)
- Kidney Research UK: https://www.kidneyresearchuk.org/transplantation/ (the native kidney position makes transplanting there difficult)
- Five kidneys (Devendra Barlewar, Delhi, Jan 2025, third transplant): https://www.thehealthsite.com/diseases-conditions/case-study-meet-devendra-barlewar-the-man-who-has-five-kidneys-in-his-body-1192950/ ; https://thepatriot.in/delhi-ncr/delhi-47-year-old-man-undergoes-rare-kidney-transplant-now-lives-with-five-kidneys-66344
- Fact sheet with hedge wording: notes/kidney-factsheet.md
